articles.title: Woman loses life savings in residency permit scam
articles.description: PORT ALDER: What began as a small consultancy fee for an elderly woman seeking a residency permit ended with her losing her life savings to scammers.
articles.content:
PORT ALDER: An elderly woman lost almost all her savings after answering an online advertisement that promised help with a residency permit.
Police said the woman first paid a small consultancy fee to a man who claimed to work for an immigration agency.
Over the next four months she was asked to make further payments for "processing", "security checks" and "bank guarantees".
She made more than 30 transfers to accounts in several names before a relative noticed and contacted the police.
District police chief Ruth Ellingham said the case was one of several similar reports this year.
"Genuine agencies never ask for repeated payments into personal accounts," she said.
Police urged anyone who believes they have been targeted to call the national fraud hotline.

articles.title: Government to replace planned monuments at historic sites
articles.description: ESTRAN: The government has proposed replacing planned statues at three historic sites with public gardens and a small museum.
articles.content:
ESTRAN: The culture ministry has proposed replacing planned statues at three historic sites with public gardens and a small museum, officials said on Saturday.
The statues had been commissioned by the previous government, but work on them had stalled since the change of government two years ago.
End of Article
